title: Skipping by the Stored Length
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean word and $p,n$ natural numbers. For every natural number $r\le n$, starting in state $4$ at the clamped input offset $p$, with a unary counter of length $n$ whose head is at $0$ and empty output, the suffix-extraction machine reaches after $r$ steps state $4$ at the clamped offset $p+r$, with the counter unchanged, its head at $r$, and output empty.
replaced:
For every $r \le n$: in the skip state with counter length $n$, $r$ steps advance
the clamped payload offset by $r$ while walking the counter head to $r$. Native
clamping makes this total even when the stored length exceeds the payload.
